solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What makes films run longer? Slumber for some bringing end sooner?

indicators.note: moving the final letter one place earlier is a small rearrangement of the word's letters

blocks.note: a dialect word for slumber, which is why the clue says 'for some'

explanation.surface: A film buff wonders whether dozing off in the cinema makes the film seem to drag on longer.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOOM has its last letter, M, moved one step forward to give SLOMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-motion playback stretches screen time, so footage shown that way lasts longer than real events did.

clue.text: Some may be persuaded by this apple punch favoured by Victoria

definitions.text: Some may be persuaded by this

blocks.note: the snow apple is a white-fleshed apple variety
Australian slang for hitting someone; Victoria is an Australian state

explanation.surface: A cider-style apple punch is said to be a favourite of Queen Victoria and a persuasive drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen, but it is the Australian state, flagging that the punch is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A snow job is a flattering, deceptive pitch meant to talk listeners round, so people may well be won over by one.

clue.text: Warning once about boxer’s top lip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around another here
in a down clue the top of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: an archaic form of alarum, an alarm or warning
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old warning about a fighter's split upper lip.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a labrum is a lip-like rim or edge, such as the upper mouthpart of an insect.

clue.text: What’s showing wavy edge round?

indicators.note: a wavy line is bent out of shape, so the word next to it is jumbled

blocks.note: a round shape is the letter O
taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what has a wavy edge running round it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: an ogee is an S-shaped curve, so an ogeed moulding shows a wavy edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogeed describes a moulding or arch with an S-shaped double curve, which reads as an undulating profile.

clue.text: Salamander placed under climbing mollusc? Mark of an illiterate activist

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a clam is a bivalve mollusc
the olm is a blind cave salamander
someone unable to write signs with a cross

explanation.surface: A nature scene with a salamander under a mollusc, then a cross signed by someone who cannot write.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm X was a prominent African-American civil-rights campaigner and Nation of Islam leader.

clue.text: China locking up referee cheating in the past

indicators.note: locking something up holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Ming porcelain is a famous kind of china
short for umpire, a referee

explanation.surface: A Chinese official imprisons a referee caught cheating years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' suggests the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumping is an obsolete word for begging or cheating, hence 'in the past'.

clue.text: What was highly predatory manner about American president?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the others

blocks.note: Latin for way or manner, as in modus operandi
standard abbreviation
the person presiding over a meeting

explanation.surface: A question about some ruthless way of behaving around a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly predatory' sounds like a description of a person; it defines an extinct animal, hence 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Machairodus is an extinct sabre-toothed cat genus, a fierce hunter of the Miocene, hence the past tense.

clue.text: African rebels stealing diamonds from girl more than once

indicators.note: stealing something from a person takes it away from them

blocks.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation
a girl's name
an instruction to write the shortened name a second time, adding no new letters

explanation.surface: Rebels repeatedly rob a girl of her diamond jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' tells you to write the shortened name twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mau Mau were Kenyan insurgents who fought British colonial rule in the 1950s.

clue.text: Might arable land be source of malt?

blocks.note: might and is both act as verbs of being in a question
a variant spelling of lea or ley, ploughable ground

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether ploughland could supply barley for malting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests barley fields; the answer is the Hebridean island famous for single-malt whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay, a Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides, has many distilleries producing peaty single malt whisky.

clue.text: Bird, name unknown, round about ten centimetres

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first pair of letters wraps the next piece

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
an abbreviation for unknown
a hand, used for measuring horses, is four inches, roughly ten centimetres

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher logs an unnamed bird only about ten centimetres long.
explanation.definitionFit: Nhandu is a variant name for the rhea, a large flightless South American ratite.

clue.text: Grade apparent risk on a single try

blocks.note: a gon or grade is a unit of angle, a hundredth of a right angle
abbreviation, as in apparent magnitude

explanation.surface: An exam result looks like a gamble staked on one attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is a card game in which a player bidding all five tricks 'goes nap'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go nap is to stake everything on one venture, from the all-or-nothing bid in the card game.

clue.text: Fly borne disease — poor horse’s one with it

blocks.note: a nag is a worn-out horse; the 's is read as 'has'
the indefinite article means one
in dialect A can stand for almost any pronoun

explanation.surface: A sorry horse has caught a disease spread by flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagana is a trypanosome infection of livestock in Africa, transmitted by the tsetse insect.

clue.text: Deformed part of engine, not behind ring

indicators.note: not tells you to leave the following word's letters out

blocks.note: the rotating shaft carrying cams
nautical for at the back
a ring shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds a bent engine part, but not the one at the back near the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deformed' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Camsho is a Scots word meaning crooked or misshapen.

clue.text: State of near neighbours shocked Candace, Cy and Jo

indicators.note: being shocked throws things into disorder, so the names are mixed up

blocks.note: the names taken letter by letter, without 'and'

explanation.surface: Three neighbours named Candace, Cy and Jo are shocked by something next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Coadjacency means being adjoining or contiguous, the condition of things lying right beside each other.

clue.text: Tapestry lacking hems, signs of unwanted modification?

indicators.note: hems are the outer edges of cloth, so losing them strips both ends off

blocks.note: Gobelin is a famous French tapestry

explanation.surface: An old wall hanging with frayed edges shows signs of tampering.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger or dash marks scribes put beside passages thought spurious, flagging interpolated text.

clue.text: Soldier left in place where Covid arose, missing wife

indicators.note: in places one item inside another
missing means going without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the Chinese city where the pandemic began
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soldier was left behind in Wuhan without his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside WUHAN to make WUHLAN, then W is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a lancer in Polish, Prussian or Austrian cavalry regiments.

clue.text: Asians sheltering continental friend with a large tent

indicators.note: sheltering something keeps it inside, so the friend sits within the people

blocks.note: the Shan are a people of Myanmar
French for friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of Asians give shelter to a friend from Europe under a big tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamiana is a large decorated canopy or marquee used in South Asia for weddings and gatherings.

clue.text: Judges approve of a fighter that’s unarmed

blocks.note: an abbreviation for the Old Testament book of Judges
to OK something is to approve it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Judges give their approval to a competitor who fights without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A judoka practises judo, a Japanese martial art of throws and holds with no weapons.

clue.text: Changing money, very little into silver and notes

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the surrounding letters

blocks.note: the chemical symbol for silver
an iota is a tiny amount
two musical notes

explanation.surface: A traveller changing currency gets very little in silver coins and banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agiotage is speculative dealing in currency exchange or stocks, from agio, a premium on exchange.

clue.text: Yielding gum to Julius with many leaflets going out together

definitions.text: with many leaflets going out together

indicators.note: something yielding gives way and can be bent into a new shape

blocks.note: every letter of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone gives Julius some gum while a plant sends out lots of leaves in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany multijugous describes a pinnate leaf bearing numerous pairs of leaflets, from Latin jugum, a yoke.

clue.text: Old wretch namely heading family on TV?

blocks.note: short for scilicet, Latin for namely
The Royle Family is a British TV sitcom about a working-class household

explanation.surface: An old misery, namely the head of a television family.
explanation.definitionFit: Scroyle is an archaic term of abuse for a scoundrel or wretch, used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Anodyne preference for speech adopting Scots mannerisms?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for the practice, the definition describes doing it

blocks.note: a balm soothes pain, as an anodyne does
orality is a focus on the spoken rather than written word

explanation.surface: A bland liking for talk that picks up Scottish ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's Scottish castle, and the word mocks Victorian enthusiasm for all things Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmorality is a mocking term for sentimental, put-on Scottishness, as fostered by Queen Victoria's Highland estate.

clue.text: Locally I rush around topping a fast time

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

blocks.note: in Scots or northern dialect I is pronounced and written as A
taken as written before mixing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local hurries round to be first to finish something quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' means sitting above in a down clue, so the jumbled word goes on top of the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashura is the tenth day of Muharram, observed by many Muslims with voluntary fasting.

clue.text: Reproduction copy needing light that holds line up

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so a letter sits within the word
in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a diazo is a copy made by a light-sensitive printing process
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A photocopier needs light, and has a line held up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozalid is a trade name for a diazo process used to reproduce plans and drawings, and for a print made that way.

clue.text: Limited consent though without substantive unanimity at first

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word surrounds the other letters
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: yet and though both mean nevertheless
a dictionary abbreviation for substantive, a noun
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Agreement given grudgingly, without real consensus behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside, an old sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-but is a qualified agreement, assent immediately followed by a reservation.

clue.text: Tower Bridge has old customs house

blocks.note: an abbreviation for bridge
standard abbreviation
an abbreviation for custom house

explanation.surface: London's Tower Bridge stands beside an old customs building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower Bridge' reads as the London landmark; the two words split into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A broch is a prehistoric circular dry-stone fortified tower found in Scotland.

clue.text: Poor man losing a son on tube

definitions.note: an adjective phrase meaning relating to a tube

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a vassal is a lowly dependant or serf
S is the abbreviation for son, and only one of them goes

explanation.surface: A poor man whose son has gone off on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests the London Underground, but it is an anatomical vessel or duct.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasal is an anatomical adjective meaning relating to a vessel or duct in the body.

clue.text: Malcolm Arnold perhaps drops mezzo-piano for Tam O’Shanter’s ride?

indicators.note: drops means lets fall, so these letters leave the word

blocks.note: Malcolm Arnold was an English writer of symphonies and film scores
the musical marking for moderately soft

explanation.surface: A composer drops a soft dynamic marking from a piece about a famous poem's horseback ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Tam O'Shanter is the hero of a Burns poem who rides home on his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooser is a Scots word for a stallion, a fitting mount for a Burns character, though Tam actually rode a mare.

clue.text: Marathon cycle rails propped up?

indicators.note: in a down clue propped up means lifted so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: the sora is a North American rail, a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A long-distance bike ride on railings that need propping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rails' means the birds, not railings.
explanation.definitionFit: The saros is the roughly eighteen-year period after which eclipses repeat, a very long astronomical recurrence.

clue.text: Aged rash formed skin fissures

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so these letters are given a new arrangement

blocks.note: every letter of the two words

explanation.surface: An old rash has developed into cracks in the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhagades are cracks or fissures in the skin, especially around the mouth, a medical term.

clue.text: Dipper — another constellation wheeling around us

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round, so the constellation is read backwards
around means surrounding, so it encloses the next word

blocks.note: Leo is a constellation, 'another' because the Dipper is one too
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stargazers see the Dipper and another constellation wheeling around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper' suggests the Big Dipper constellation, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel or water ouzel is an old name for the dipper, a bird that bobs and dives in streams.

clue.text: Anzac’s worn-out during following conflict

indicators.note: following places the word for during after the word for conflict, not before it

blocks.note: a war is an armed conflict
as in 'by day', meaning during the day

explanation.surface: An Australian soldier is exhausted during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: An Anzac is an Australian or New Zealand soldier, so the definition is a word used down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Warby is Australian slang for shabby, scruffy or decrepit.

clue.text: Insensitive about one concept in grammar

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the adjective wraps around a letter

blocks.note: crass means tactless and insensitive
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone tactless with an idea about grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Crasis is the contraction of two vowels across a word boundary into one long vowel, especially in Greek.

clue.text: Waterproof with hood ready inside infant’s cap

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a caul is the membrane sometimes covering a newborn's head
as in 'all systems go', meaning ready

explanation.surface: A rain jacket with a hood, ready to put on over a baby's bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infant's cap' suggests a woolly hat, but it is the birth membrane.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoul is a lightweight hooded anorak that keeps out rain, usually pulled on over the head.

clue.text: Holiday drink? God, finally, yes

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a half is half a pint of beer
the closing letter of the word
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday is offered a drink and says yes at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-day is a break from work lasting the afternoon or morning, a short leave period.

clue.text: Mostly idle jester

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to fester can mean to lie idle and rot

explanation.definitionFit: Feste is the clown or fool in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, Olivia's household entertainer.
